job: Move from one page to the next with the chrome held still and only the content changing.
purpose: A stylesheet and a helper, not a component. Under <html data-fd-transition> the sidebar, top bar and other chrome keep their own names and do not fade, while the page fades (fade), slides along the inline axis (slide) or stays (none). transition(update, { kind, direction }) sets the attribute while it runs, for a single-page route change. A multi-page site opts in by linking fire/transitions.css, setting the attribute and marking its module scripts blocking="render".
useWhen: A multi-page site or the Ember templates should feel like one app when a link is followed.
A single-page app swaps a route and the shell should stay put.
A phone drill-down should slide forward and reverse on back.

avoidWhen.when: One part of a page changes in place: a tab panel, a filter result, a skeleton becoming content.
A surface appears over the page, such as a dialog, a sheet or a menu.
The page must swap at once, for example a sign-out.

states.name: no support
states.how: the browser has no View Transitions: the page loads as usual and transition() calls update at once

states.name: reduced motion
states.how: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce opts no page in; transition() only calls update

states.name: motion none
states.how: the motion dial at none (--fd-motion 0): the durations are zero and transition() only calls update

states.name: back
states.how: data-fd-direction="back" on <html> while a slide runs; set by the module, never by hand

variants.useWhen: Pages at one level of the app; the default.
A phone drill-down that goes deeper and back.
A page or a single link that must swap at once.
